name: Maoch
overview: Maoch is a male figure known primarily as the father of the king of Gath, as recorded in 1 Samuel 27:2. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no additional information about his tribe or other personal details. His mention is brief and serves to identify his son within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Maoch means "poor one" and is a proper name not given by God, according to 1 Samuel 27:2. Another related name, Maacah, possibly means "dull, stupid" and appears in 1 Kings 2:39, although this name is distinct from Maoch and is mentioned separately in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Maoch as the father of Achish, the king of Gath, based on an inferred relationship from 1 Samuel 27:2. No other family relationships are explicitly documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Maoch's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his identification as the father of Achish, a Philistine king of Gath who interacts with David during his time of refuge. Though Maoch himself does not play an active role, his mention provides a genealogical anchor that helps situate Achish within the historical and cultural context of the Philistine cities. This connection aids in understanding the political landscape surrounding David's experiences.
